summary: Lens-lantern light on Round Island in the St. Marys River, lit 1892; unattended from 1922-23 and privately owned, with no public access.

lens.where: not stated; LHF says the lens lantern was still in place in 1909

structures.note: Eight-foot-square tower on a one-and-a-half-story frame dwelling. LHF gives the tower as 40 feet; USLHS gives 35 feet from base to lantern centre and 40 feet as the height of the light above water. Light moved to a steel tower 65 yards north on 30 June 1923 (LHF).
Acetylene light moved here from the dwelling lantern on 30 June 1923 (LHF).

access.note: Privately owned. LHF says the lighthouse is best viewed from the St. Marys River. USLHS lists the station as not open to the public.

events.note: Act approved 3 March 1891 appropriated $30,000 for lights and ranges from Pipe Island to Sault Ste. Marie.
Deed to a one-acre parcel on the island's east side obtained 5 May 1892 (LHF).
First exhibited 20 September 1892 (LHF; USLHS station established 1892).
Original optic was a lens lantern (USLHS). LHF: U.S.-made lens lanterns used because of delays in procuring lenses from abroad.
Cedar Point Range location changed to Round Island; new range on Round Island completed and in commission (Commissioner 1920; Bulletin 1920).
Characteristic changed to a white flash every two seconds (LHF).
Round Island converted to an unattended acetylene light (Commissioner 1922; Bulletin 1922 says changed to acetylene).
Light moved from the dwelling lantern to a steel tower 65 yards north on 30 June 1923; station unattended (LHF).
Around 1998 a private buyer became the lighthouse's third private owner (LHF; approximate).

corrections.why: USLHS gives the height of light above mean high water as 40 feet (12.2 m). The record's 8.5 m is not supported by a source read here. Check the Light List before accepting.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1922 date (Wikidata) matches the Commissioner's 1922 report of the conversion to an unattended acetylene light; the 1923 date (Rowlett) matches LHF's move to the steel tower and the station becoming unattended. No source read describes a shutdown, so no deactivation date is proposed.

LHF gives the tower as 40 feet; USLHS gives 35 feet from base to lantern centre (10.7 m, matching the record's 10.7 m structure height) and 40 feet as the height of the light above water (12.2 m, matching focal_height_m). Both are stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: 1) Round Island is in three sources that are easy to confuse: this St. Marys River light (1892, Chippewa County); the Round Island light in the Straits of Mackinac; and Round Island off Pascagoula, Mississippi (keepers Brouwer, Schreiber, Steiner and Portman in the Bulletin and Commissioner entries). Only entries naming the St. Marys River or Chippewa County were used. 2) No storms, wrecks or rescues at this station were found in the corpus for the St. Marys station. The Bulletin's 1924 to 1929 index lists 'Round Island light station' keeper assists and a rescue (pages 69, 152, 219, 232, 268) and 'Ryan, Tony, asst keeper Round Island' (page 152); these are not checked and are probably the Straits station, since this station was unattended from 1922-23. LHF's claim that Richardson helped repair patrol boat S.P. 309 in 1918 was not found in the 1918 Bulletin text searched; not used. 3) Keepers before 1896 are not named by any source read; the station was first lit in September 1892. 4) Light status now: unknown. USLHS records 'Active Aid to Navigation? No' and the record says 'inactive'; the Commissioner and Bulletin describe an acetylene light that remained lit after 1922. Check the Coast Guard list of lights (LLNR 7-12940). 5) The record's 'boat_only: true' is not confirmed by any source read; LHF says the lighthouse is best viewed from the river. 6) The owner named by LHF is a private person and is not named here. 7) LHF gives a 2016 and 2021 asking price; the story gives both as sale listings with no date for the current owner. 8) Photos: the record's Commons photo has no licence and is not added. 9) The 1920 'Cedar Point Range to Round Island' change: the Commissioner does not say whether this range is on the island or in the channel; the story says only that a new range was completed on Round Island. 10) The 1918 Richardson line is printed in the Commissioner's table of saving of life and property (scan p. 367). Name and station are on one printed line, but the service column is separate in the OCR, so the story says only that the table names him and does not describe a rescue. The page image was not viewed. 11) The record's 'deactivated' events (1922 Wikidata; 1923 Rowlett) are not supported as shutdown dates by the sources read; see resolved_conflicts. 12) The fiscal-year titles were corrected after the report headers were checked: the 1891 Light-House Board volume is for the year ended 30 June 1891 (not '1891 to 1892').
